2.0.6 Premature retirement costs/redundancy costs (new provisions)

Any budget for payments to be made by the local authority in respect of the dismissal, or for the purpose of securing the resignation, of any member of the staff of the school, after 1 April 2025 under section 37, Education Act 2002.

This line is meant to be for new costs in the financial year, in this case 2025 to 2026. For old costs please record in line 2.3.3 (‘Pension costs, includes existing early retirement costs’).

2.0.7 Monitoring national curriculum assessment

Record expenditure on monitoring national curriculum assessment arrangements required by orders made under section 87 of the Education Act 2002.

2.1.1 Educational psychology service

All expenditure on educational psychology services should be entered here.

The cost of educational psychology (EP) services should not be apportioned elsewhere unless an educational psychologist is specially appointed to undertake an alternative function (for example, managing the behaviour support service).

Expenditure on EP bespoke/commissioned work in behaviour support should go into line 1.1.2 ‘Behaviour support services’.

2.1.2 SEN administration, assessment, coordination and monitoring

Include here expenditure on identification and assessment of children with SEN and disability; information about the local offer to children with SEN; and the making, maintaining and reviewing of EHC plans under section 36 to 45 of the Children and Families Act 2014. Include the cost of responding to SEN complaints, including tribunal appeals.

Include the cost of strategic management and planning of services to support the inclusion and attainment of children and young people with SEN, preparing relevant strategic plans, SEN administration, planning and coordination.

rates for the provider types you are delivering funded places through for eligible working parents of children aged 9 months to 2 years. Please note all local authorities must use a universal base rate of funding for all providers.

Amount and unit

Please record here the total number of hours you expect to fund in the financial year for the eligible working parents of children aged 9 months to 2 years entitlement, split by provider type. The unit value entered for base rates must be an hourly rate. The unit value column is not fixed to hourly rate in COLLECT, therefore please make sure only the ‘per hour’ unit is entered.

Supplements

Please provide a short explanation of your supplement payments.

We have included the permitted discretionary early years supplements (deprivation, quality, flexibility, rurality/sparsity and English as an additional language) in the proforma. If you do not use supplements for the working parents of children aged 9 months to 2 years entitlement, leave the relevant rows blank.

Description

In the description, please specify what each of the different supplements are paid for. Please include all supplements for each of the factors, including what the qualifying criteria are for each of your different supplements (adding more lines if necessary). For example, if the supplements differ for different providers, use separate rows for each provider with a brief description of what they are paid for.

Amount and unit

The amount for supplements can either be an hourly rate, a rate per child or a lump sum. In the amount column, please record the funding paid to providers and in the unit column, use the dropdown box to select whether this amount is per hour, per child or a lump sum.

Percentage of funding provided through supplements

Please note, the total value of supplements used must not be more than 12.0% of the total value of planned funding to be passed through to providers for delivering the government entitlement hours. This row is calculated automatically so you can determine compliance on the 12% supplement funding cap. To be compliant, the funding provided through supplements cannot be more than 12%. That is, rounding down 12.4% will not be considered as meeting the requirement. The supplements funding percentage will be shown to 1 decimal place in the early years proforma. You can view the calculated supplements percentage when you download the ‘EY proforma table’ report in COLLECT.

Further details on how this is calculated is included in the early years entitlements operational guide.

Total funding for early years local funding formula for working parents of 9-month to 2-year-olds

This row is calculated automatically.

Special educational needs inclusion fund (SENIF) (funding paid directly to providers)

Local authorities should establish SENIFs for all children with SEN, who are eligible for or taking up any of the early years entitlements. The SENIF is to resource and support the needs of individual children with low-level SEN.

The SENIF can be used in the form of additional funding paid directly to providers for supporting children with SEN; or centrally used to support specialist local authority SEN services in the local area.

This column should only be used to record the amount of funding paid directly to providers for SENIF.

Please note, only the amount paid directly to providers for SENIF will be considered within the 96% pass-through rate calculation. Therefore, only include the planned budget you intend to directly fund providers here. If you plan to use any of the SENIF funding for providing in-kind SEN specialist support to providers, this should be budgeted under central spend (section 13 of the early years table).

Description

Whilst some local authorities may choose to pool funding and hold one SENIF for use across all of the early years entitlements, the notional amount allocated to be spent on children accessing an entitlement should be broken down and recorded against the respective entitlement funding stream, i.e., a quantity given for SENIF funding for each of the entitlements. This is because the pass-through calculation will be applied to each individual funding stream. A description of what the qualifying criteria are for your local SENIF, should also be included, adding additional rows for different criteria if necessary.

Amount

In the amount column please record the planned budget for the SENIF funding paid directly to providers, split by provider type. Since local authorities can pool funding from either or both of their early years and high needs DSG funding blocks, please provide a breakdown of the amount set aside for the SENIF from the 2 funding blocks – separate rows are included in early years table sections 11a, 11b, 11c and 11d to record the amounts allocated from the different blocks.

The budget (sections 11a, 11b, 11c and 11d of the early years table) for each entitlement will be counted within the high pass-through rate funding calculation for the respective funding stream.

Total funding for SENIF (funding paid directly to providers)

This row is calculated for each entitlement automatically.

Early years contingency funding

Please briefly explain what you include in contingency funding for each of the entitlements and the amounts allocated to it. Contingency funding should be recorded separately for children aged 9 months to 2 years, 2-year-olds from families receiving additional support, the working parents of 2-year-olds and for 3- and 4-year-olds, with a comprehensive breakdown as far as possible of what the contingency funding is intended to cover (add more lines if necessary).

This expenditure will also need to be included in line 1.3.1 – ‘Central expenditure on early years entitlement’.

Please note, contingency funding will be counted within the pass-through rate for providers.

For places in special units and resourced provision attached to mainstream schools, the total cost of the places should be £6,000 multiplied by the number of places funded at that rate, and £10,000 multiplied by the number of places funded at that rate. The only exception is where the place amount is reduced because the unit or resourced provision is opening or closing during the financial year. When the place numbers change in September 2025, multiply the place number for the period April to August 2025 by £2,500 (five-twelfths of £6,000) or £4,167 (five-twelfths of £10,000), and the place number for the period September 2025 to March 2026 by £3,500 (seven-twelfths of £6,000) or £5,833 (seven-twelfths of £10,000) to get the total for the financial year April 2025 to March 2026.

AP places

April 2025 to August 2025

September 2025 to March 2026

Include the number of places to provide AP for pupils at £10,000 per place per annum.

AP place funding

April 2025 to March 2026

This is the total cost of the places in the previous columns. Multiply the place number for the period April to August 2025 by £4,167 (five-twelfths of £10,000), and the place number for the period September 2025 to March 2026 by £5,833 (seven-twelfths of £10,000) to get the total for the financial year April 2025 to March 2026. The only exception to this calculation is where the place amounts are reduced because the school is opening or closing during the financial year.

Hospital education places

April 2025 to August 2025

September 2025 to March 2026

Hospital education places must be funded at the same per place amount as in 2024 to 2025, unless the authority has decided to increase the amount. Hospital education is defined as where the child is being provided with such education by reason of a decision made by a medical practitioner (as opposed to by an educationalist).

The funding for the number of hospital education places in special schools (including so-called hospital schools) or PRUs (sometimes known as medical PRUs) is the amount which must be included in line 1.0.2. It should exclude expenditure on hospital education services that are not funded as places at these providers, which should instead be included in line 1.2.6. Please note that there should be no duplication of hospital education place funding included in the high needs places table and the amounts in line 1.2.6 of the local authority table, as the place funding should be included in line 1.0.2.

Where appropriate, the funding for hospital education places should also include any high needs funding paid to maintained special schools and PRUs providing hospital education, for teachers’ pay and pensions (employer contributions) costs, under the additional condition of grant attached to local authorities’ DSG (section 3.6(6)).

Hospital education place funding

April 2025 to March 2026

Total cost of the places in the previous column. This should be the amount per place multiplied by the number of places in the previous columns. See above for how to work out the amount for the financial year April 2025 to March 2026 if the place number changes in September 2025.

Total high needs place funding net

April 2025 to March 2026

Total high needs place funding for the institution (the sum of the columns for SEN place funding, AP place funding and hospital education place funding).

The early years collection and the proforma

This section of the return records the total local authority DSG spending on early years, including:

the universal 15 hours entitlement for 3- and 4-year-olds

the additional 15 hours for eligible working parents of 3- and 4-year-olds

the 15 hours entitlement for 2-year-olds from families receiving additional support (formerly referred to as the ‘disadvantaged 2-year-olds entitlement’)

the 15 hours entitlement for eligible working parents of 2-year-olds (increasing to 30 hours from September 2025)

the 15 hours entitlement for eligible working parents of 9 month to 2-year-olds (increasing to 30 hours from September 2025)

supplementary funding for maintained nursery schools

any budget allocated for the early years SEN inclusion fund

EYPP

DAF

any other DSG expenditure on early years

The planned budget information from section 251 will be used to monitor compliance with all the early years funding rules. Further details about the funding rules is available in the early years entitlements operational guide for local authorities.

The early years entitlement information recorded on COLLECT will be output into the early years proforma. The proforma is split into the:

local funding formula for 3- and 4-year-olds (for both the universal 15 hours and additional 15 hours)

local funding formula for 2-year-olds from families receiving additional support

local funding formula for working parents of 2-year-olds

local funding formula for working parents of 9 month to 2-year-olds

special educational needs inclusion fund (SENIF) – funding paid directly to providers

contingency and centrally retained spending

EYPP

DAF

Each section on local funding formulae and funding paid directly to providers for SENIF is also split into provider types, giving data for maintained nursery schools, nursery classes and PVI settings.

DfE will publish the early years proforma for each local authority as part of the early years benchmarking information later in the year.
